title: CapabilityContract
description: The full shape docs/SPEC.md section 1 sketches, as an actual JSON Schema document (docs/ROADMAP.md Phase 1, item 1's 'not just the prose shape already written'). This is the ASPIRATIONAL shape: no Skill in the ecosystem publishes every field below yet (see docs/ROADMAP.md Phase 2 and registry/README.md's 'What this deliberately is not'). `required` below is deliberately narrow -- only what every real Skill's `contract --json` / `<skill> contract --json` output already carries today, per registry/contract.py and registry/tests/fixtures/*.provides.json -- so this schema both documents the target shape in full AND validates today's real, minimal contracts without rejecting any of them. The richer per-`provides`-entry fields stay optional until a real Skill publishes them (VISION, per registry/README.md), at which point they become checkable, not just described.

skill_id.description: Existing: flat top-level skill identity, used by 8 of 10 audited Skills (docs/SPEC.md section 1; docs/POC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACT.md Finding 9). One of skill_id / id / skill.id must be present -- see this schema's top-level anyOf.

id.description: Existing: transcription-skill's outlier flat identity field (no skill_id at all). Not part of docs/SPEC.md's original sketch, but real (registry/contract.py's skill_identity()).

skill.description: Existing: ffmpeg-skill's nested skill-metadata shape (docs/POC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACT.md Finding 7) instead of flat top-level fields.

version.description: Existing: every repo's own version field. Renamed from an earlier 'skill_version' draft -- no real Skill uses that name, they all say 'version' (docs/SPEC.md section 1; docs/POC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACT.md Finding 1).

contract_version.description: Existing, inconsistently typed today (e.g. "1.0" for ffmpeg-skill, 1 for qc-skill). docs/VERSIONING.md deliberately does not mandate a version-string format.

provides.description: The Capability ids this Skill publishes (docs/SPEC.md section 1; named 'provides', not 'capabilities', to avoid colliding with several Skills' pre-existing environment-capability-detection field of that name -- see docs/SPEC.md section 1's naming note).

dependencies.description: Existing pattern: every delegating Skill's adapter.py declares this against another Skill's contract_version (docs/VERSIONING.md), e.g. depends on ffmpeg-skill >=0.9.1,<1.0.0.

version_range.description: A contract_version range (e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'), never an exact pin -- docs/VERSIONING.md section 3. No mandated format (not necessarily SemVer).

not_provided.description: Existing: ffmpeg-skill's manifest of self-declared non-responsibilities.

CapabilityId.description: The dotted `<domain>.<verb>` namespace docs/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md section 1 proposes, e.g. 'edit.trim', 'color.primary_correction'. Not machine-enforced beyond non-empty: real ids also include Skill-name-prefixed forms like 'ffmpeg-skill.audio' -- no single regex covers every real id in the ecosystem today without either rejecting a real one or accepting nonsense, so this stays a plain non-empty string rather than a guessed pattern.

ProvidesEntry.description: One published Capability. `id`, `lifecycle` and `tool_id` are required because every real Skill's provides[] entry already carries exactly these three (registry/contract.py's validate_provides_entry()) -- the richer fields below are docs/SPEC.md section 1's aspirational per-capability shape, PROPOSED, not yet published by any Skill in the ecosystem (registry/README.md).

tool_id.description: Existing: every real Skill's provides[] entry also carries this, bridging the Capability id to the underlying CLI tool it maps to (e.g. 'qc/run', 'ffmpeg-skill/audio') -- not in docs/SPEC.md's original sketch by this name, but universal in practice.

input_schema.description: PROPOSED (docs/SPEC.md section 1): typed params, closed vocabulary. Existing in every repo's contract.py in some form, but not yet expressed per-Capability in this exact shape by any Skill.

output_schema.description: PROPOSED (docs/SPEC.md section 1): existing in ffmpeg-skill's ToolSpec output_schema, not yet universal.

input_artifact_types.description: PROPOSED (docs/SPEC.md section 1): generalizes each Skill's existing but differently-shaped inputs/outputs fields.

mutates_input.description: Existing: ffmpeg-skill + others already publish this, always false today, everywhere.

security.description: PROPOSED (docs/SPEC.md section 1): today reimplemented ad hoc per repo, not yet published under this exact key by any Skill.
